title: American civics
description: How the United States government is built, and how the Constitution limits it.

ideas.title: The Constitution
ideas.summary: Written in 1787, the Constitution is the supreme law; it divides power among branches and between nation and states.

items.q: In what year was the United States Constitution written, at the convention in Philadelphia?
What are the first three words of the United States Constitution?
What is the term for the division of power between the national government and the states in the United States?
Which clause of the US Constitution makes it, and federal law, the "supreme Law of the Land"?
items.a: The Supremacy Clause, in Article VI

ideas.title: Three branches
ideas.summary: Congress makes the laws, the president carries them out, the courts interpret them, and each checks the others.

items.q: What are the three branches of the United States federal government?
What is the name for the system in which each branch of the US government can limit the power of the others?
Which 1803 Supreme Court case established judicial review, the power to strike down laws as unconstitutional?
How many justices sit on the United States Supreme Court?

ideas.title: Congress
ideas.summary: Congress has two chambers: a House sized by population and a Senate with two members for every state.

items.q: How many voting members does the US House of Representatives have?
How many senators does the United States have, and how many come from each state?
How long are the terms of a US representative and a US senator?
items.a: Two years for a representative, six years for a senator

items.q: Which chamber of Congress confirms presidential appointments and approves treaties?

ideas.title: How a bill becomes law
ideas.summary: A bill must pass the House and the Senate in identical form, then be signed by the president or survive a veto.

items.q: In which chamber of Congress must bills for raising revenue begin?
What must happen to a bill in Congress before it can be sent to the president?
items.a: Both the House and the Senate must pass it in identical form

items.q: What vote does Congress need to override a presidential veto?
items.a: Two-thirds of both the House and the Senate

items.q: What is a pocket veto?
items.a: An unsigned bill dies because Congress adjourned during the president's ten days to act on it

ideas.title: The Bill of Rights
ideas.summary: The first ten amendments, ratified in 1791, protect individual liberties from the power of government.

items.q: What name is given to the first ten amendments to the US Constitution, and in what year were they ratified?
items.a: The Bill of Rights, ratified in 1791

items.q: Which amendment to the US Constitution protects freedom of religion, speech, the press, assembly and petition?
Which amendment to the US Constitution protects against unreasonable searches and seizures?
Which amendment to the US Constitution protects a person from being forced to testify against themselves?

ideas.title: Later amendments
ideas.summary: Amendments after the Civil War ended slavery, promised equal protection and steadily widened the right to vote.

items.q: What did the Thirteenth Amendment to the US Constitution do, in 1865?
Which amendment to the US Constitution, ratified in 1868, defines citizenship and guarantees equal protection of the laws?
Which amendment to the US Constitution guaranteed women the right to vote, and in what year was it ratified?
What fraction of the states must ratify an amendment to the US Constitution?
